quote: Theorem 1. For two parallel systems with component lifetimes being distributed as (X1, X2) ~ MOE(λ1, λ2, λ3) and (Y1, Y2) ~ MOE(µ1, µ2, λ3), the following implication holds: ((λ1 + λ3)−1, (λ2 + λ3)−1) ⪰^m ((µ1 + λ3)−1, (µ2 + λ3)−1) ⇒ X2:2 ≥mrl Y2:2.
family: Marshall–Olkin bivariate exponential MOE(λ1,λ2,λ3): F̄(x1,x2) = exp{−(λ1 x1 + λ2 x2 + λ3 (x1 ∨ x2))}
compared: X2:2 (parallel system of MOE pair) vs Y2:2, sharing common λ3

hypotheses.text: (X1, X2) ~ MOE(λ1, λ2, λ3) and (Y1, Y2) ~ MOE(µ1, µ2, λ3)
hypotheses.formal: MOE pairs with shared shock rate λ3
vector of marginal means majorizes the other

ambiguity: Symbol verified via PDF rendering: ⪰^m (majorization). Condition couples marginal means rather than marginal rates.

quote: Theorem 2. For η ∈ Θn(θ), we have R(X, n) ≥st R(Y, n). [with Θn(θ) = {η = (η1,...,ηn) ∈ En+ : θ ⪰^p η and θk ≥ ηk for k = 2,...,n}, where X1,...,Xn are independent exponential with hazard rates θ1,...,θn, Y1,...,Yn independent exponential with hazard rates η1,...,ηn, and R(X,n) = Xn:n − X1:n is the sample range]
family: Independent exponential variables with hazard rates θi (for X) and ηi (for Y); En+ = {x ∈ Rn : 0 < x1 ≤ ... ≤ xn}
compared: R(X,n) vs R(Y,n), hazard-rate vectors θ vs η

hypotheses.text: X1,...,Xn independent exponential with hazard rates θi; Y's likewise with rates ηi
η ∈ Θn(θ): θ ⪰^p η (p-majorization) and θk ≥ ηk for k = 2,...,n
hypotheses.formal: θ p-majorizes η (Π θ_(j) ≤ Π η_(j) by Definition 2(iii) reading 'a is said to p-majorize b' for θ vs η) plus componentwise domination of all but the smallest rate

ambiguity: Symbol verified via PDF rendering: ⪰^p = p-majorization with θ the majorizing (more spread) vector.
